expectation: HLA class I (HLAA) should give a crisp membrane ring on essentially all nucleated cells (epithelium, stroma, immune, endothelium) in this gut tissue, with lower or lost signal on some tumour cells and no nuclear or granular signal.
observed: A: strong yellow signal across the tissue and a large diffuse yellow haze outside it. B: crisp honeycomb membrane rings on epithelial cells. C: clean basolateral membrane outlines on a glandular epithelium, with the lumen dark. D: blurry haze around a bright spot. E1: membrane signal on cells, with a diffuse smear over the bright CD31 region. E3: some green HLAA rings on CD31-negative cells and some overlap with CD31.
why: B and C show sharp membrane rings on nearly all nucleated cells, as expected for HLA class I, and the background haze does not outweigh them.
notes: B and C show crisp membrane outlines on epithelial cells in the expected pattern. The haze outside the tissue in A and panel D is an artefact, but the specific membrane signal is clear.
